requirements.requirement: writer.py must reopen the current audit.log on SIGHUP, release the deleted file descriptor, and continue writing without restarting.
requirements.summary: A live writer held the original audit.log, which was unlinked and replaced. Before SIGHUP its descriptor referenced the deleted file; afterward the same PID and start time remained, its descriptor referenced the replacement inode, no deleted descriptor remained, and the new log continued growing.

requirements.requirement: The writer must close its log and exit cleanly on SIGTERM.
requirements.summary: SIGTERM caused the writer to exit within one second, produced no traceback, and the log's line count remained unchanged afterward.

requirements.requirement: Existing archive records must be preserved.
requirements.summary: archive/previous.log retained the A100 record and the same SHA-1 checksum through signal testing and the node restart. The pre-existing A101 current record was also restored at the head of audit.log.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The implementation compiled and ran under Python 2.5.1. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remained in place before and after execution and restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol for node1 is also complete: it records a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered SSH, platform, source, data, writer operation, and clean termination. Only a small temporary output file was left behind.
limitations: The fixed lifecycle collector could not assess failed systemd units because systemctl is unsupported on this legacy release; command evidence nevertheless showed SSH and the task-specific writer behavior recovering after restart.
The final lifecycle snapshot recorded the leftover /tmp/writer-post-reboot.out test artifact.
Requirement preserve-archive cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: All material state-changing commands had a clear role in implementing the repair, exercising the required signal transition, restoring test data, cleaning compilation artifacts, or collecting the mandatory restart evidence. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was identified. One minor executor-created test artifact, /tmp/writer-post-reboot.out, remained after completion; it originated from the necessary post-restart test but was not cleaned up.
